hypothesis: Generating questions one at a time, each conditioned on the already-asked set, should push the 3B off its modal cluster and into the task-specific tail of its distribution — because forcing explicit novelty relative to prior questions changes the generation dynamic in a way that flat single-call emission cannot.
technique: Eight sequential on-device model calls (1 framing + 7 question calls) built on the exp003 RAG few-shot base; each question call receives the already-asked questions in-context and is instructed to probe a genuinely different unknown, aiming to prevent modal collapse through explicit per-step novelty conditioning.
result: Scored 0.245 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), −0.075 below the exp003/exp011 best of ~0.32 and −0.062 below the 0.307 baseline — discarded. Coverage stayed pinned at 3, naturalness dropped to 3 (robotic yes/no status checks), and nonRed regressed to 3 despite the explicit do-not-repeat conditioning, with the judge flagging severe near-duplicate pairs across multiple tasks; the hypothesis was fully falsified, as sequential novelty conditioning neither pushed into the task-specific tail nor bought the non-redundancy it structurally promised.
